does your coding agent get worse as its context fills up?
Does your agent get worse as its context fills?
Each row: a slice of how full the context window was, and how often the agent slipped there.
A slip = a failed edit, a repeated tool call, a re-read, an “actually, let me fix that,” or a tool error.
green = healthy zone · red = past your threshold · “give-or-take” = 95% confidence range
A “reversal” is the agent undoing or contradicting itself — a failed edit, a retry after an error,
or an “actually, let me fix that.” This asks: once a session already has a few reversals,
does the very next step fail more often?
→ Yes, mistakes snowball: after a few reversals the next step fails far more often.
Starting a fresh session breaks the spiral.
Fresh fail = slip rate when the context is nearly empty · Deep fail = when it's nearly full
Ratio = Deep ÷ Fresh (1× = no rot, higher = worse) · Threshold = fill where slips start climbing
